newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade student protesters suffer setback.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade student protesters suffer setback.

text.p: Students protesting against election fraud in Serbia suffered a setback on Wednesday when Belgrade University rejected one of their key demands by refusing to sack the institution's rector.
The university Council voted 41 to 25 to throw out a no-confidence motion in the rector, Dragutin Velickovic, the council chairman said.

The university council's decision was taken despite a promise by President Slobodan Milosevic's government to grant what the students demanded. Two Serbian deputy prime ministers signed a statement to that effect on Saturday.

The students have been demonstrating separately from the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition for the past 59 days against the annulment of opposition victories in Serbia's 14 biggest cities at November 17 local elections.

Electoral officials in Belgrade and Serbia's second city of Nis have reinstated Zajedno's election victories, but a senior hardliner in the ruling Socialists said on Wednesday an appeal was planned against the decision affecting the capital.

The students are demanding reinstatement of all Zajedno's poll victories. They also want those involved in election fraud to be punished, free access to media and the sacking of Belgrade University's rector.
